thread:
olivia: Hi runtime — prepping the blog/launch post. We need an auditable, tiny benchmark pack that marketing can attach to the post and internal methodology note. Goal: no cherry-picking, reproducible, and a single-share PNG for the post.

olivia: Core asks (short):
- Warmup run: ramp 20rps -> 150rps over 4m (linear) with small poisson jitter, hold 150rps for 9m, ~10k total. Provide p50/p95/p99 and full time series.

- Coldstart sweep: 4k independent single-shot requests against new replicas, produce latency bucket heatmap and raw csv.

- Quant coverage: fp16, q4_0, q5_1 (if q5_1 fails OOM note fallback).

- Long-context tail: 12k-token prompts (40 samples), run both cold KV and warm KV.

- Stream vs non-stream quick compare (12 samples each).

- Provide a samples_manifest.json with sample IDs, seed used, and md5 of the payload file for provenance.

rahul: Which exact model name are we using? Also prefer a deterministic seed for sampling.

olivia: Use the product-landing model: "redwood-x-7b-lm". Use seed=1337 for sampling from marketing_cohort_v4. Include sample IDs in the manifest so we can reproduce.

diego: We'll run this on pool-4. Plan to schedule three jobs: job-warmup-12321, job-cold-12322, job-quant-12323. Artifacts will be uploaded to s3://internal-bench/marketing/1767000000/. We'll include md5 checksums for each artifact.

sophie: Product needs: warmup_timeseries.csv, coldstart_heatmap.png, quant_summary.csv (include p50/p95/p99 and peak memory), long_context_breakdown.csv, samples_manifest.json, runbook.txt, and a single PNG (warmup_small.png) sized for the blog.

rahul: For warmup distribution, you asked for poisson jitter — confirm we should use linear ramp + poisson noise. Also do you want requests to reuse context across consecutive requests (session) or all independent?

olivia: Linear ramp + poisson jitter is perfect. For warmup use independent sessions so we illustrate typical multi-tenant behavior. For long-context tests include both independent and session-follow-up (warm cache).

diego: Example curl we'll add to manifest (token redacted):

```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-x-7b-lm","input":"<sample>","max_tokens":1024,"stream":false,"cache_kv":false}'
```

diego: ETA full artifacts 24-36h. If you need a preview image earlier I can run a smaller 1k-request warmup_preview and drop warmup_preview.png by EOD.

olivia: Preview would help with copy review. Also: embargo until launch week. Mark any runs that used experimental kernels/flags as EXPERIMENTAL in the manifest.

rahul: We'll also record exact infra (instance type, driver, CUDA versions) and kernel flags in runbook.txt for audit. Include peak GPU mem per variant.

bench-bot: job-warmup-12321 queued on pool-4 (estimated runtime ~90m). Logs: https://internal.redwood/bench/runs/12321. Artifacts target: s3://internal-bench/marketing/1767000000/.

diego: I'll ping this channel with the S3 paths and MD5s when uploads finish and tag @olivia @sophie. If any quant variant OOMs or shows a >10% perf regression vs fp16 we'll call it out in the summary and provide fallback details.

olivia: Perfect, thanks. Please ensure samples_manifest.json includes exact sampling query, seed, and the path to the raw sample file so legal can audit provenance later.

bench-bot: job-quant-12323 queued. Notifying participants on job completion.
